resources.string: Host support currently covers Douyin, com.ss.android.ugc.aweme, only. Patching any other app does not give it host features that have not been implemented.
Embeds the NukeApp-OSS module in the target APK, signs it on this device and exports the result.
A single local APK file is supported. Prepare the complete APK first; split APKs, APKS and XAPK are not supported yet.
Embeds the chosen NukeApp-OSS module file
Signing key generated on this device

The module file and the target file are imported separately. NukeApp-OSS does not need to be installed and nothing connects to the network; the chosen files stay unchanged, and the result is exported separately.

The patched APK is signed again with this device\'s key, so it usually cannot be installed over an existing install with a different signature; the app\'s signature checks, sign-in or data migration may also be affected. This tool never uninstalls an app or clears its data.
The module and the target are both analyzed; patching can start.
Export it and install it yourself. Actual compatibility still has to be verified inside the target app.
The operation could not be completed. Check the log and try again.
You can choose the module or the target APK again; when both files are analyzed, patching can be retried.

Requires Android 9 or later and a 4 KiB page size. A generated, signed and verified APK does not mean the Hook is in effect inside the target app; compatibility after installing has to be verified separately.
A standalone, local APK patching tool.
This app does the patching, signing and file verification. The imported NukeApp-OSS module reaches the host through libxposed API 102 and keeps its own scope and Hook scheduling.
Follows and reuses LSPatch for APK patching and module embedding, keeping the upstream license and attribution. Patching runs on this device and the chosen APKs are never uploaded.
Verifying the file, payload and signature independently…
The patched, signed APK was exported; install it yourself.
The file could not be exported. Check the destination, write permission and free space. You can choose an export location again to retry.
Not completed. See the message on the page and try again.
The APK file component could not be loaded. Make sure this install is complete and supports this device\'s architecture, then restart NukePatcher and try again.
Writing and signing the APK; a large file may take a while…
This version cannot patch on a device with a 16 KiB page size yet. The upstream ZIP payload is only aligned to 4 KiB.
Choose a complete single APK. Split APKs, a base APK that depends on splits and APK sets are not supported yet.
NukeApp-OSS and NukePatcher cannot be patch targets. Choose another target APK.
Patch mode requires Android 9 or later, and the target APK\'s minimum system cannot be newer than this device.
The file is unusable or failed verification. Make sure it is a complete, unpatched APK and check the free storage space.
The source is the local file you choose. Export it from the NukeApp-OSS home page or pick a downloaded module package; the identity and entry checks do not authenticate the file\'s publisher.
The chosen file is not a compatible, complete NukeApp-OSS module APK. Check the package name, the API 102 entry and the module configuration, and do not choose the patcher or a patched app.
Patching changes the install signature, so the result usually cannot be installed over the original app.
Patching can start once the module and the target are both chosen.
After patching and verification, export the APK here.
